items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: Kid Ory comes by and he said, 'Oh, man. This ain't the type of music I want to hear.' ... But I mean, we fixed him later on. ... Kid Ory hit the ceiling, you know. ... he let know he didn't like me. He wouldn't say nothin' to me

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Because Hawk had a big influence on Jazz. Well, that's no more than right, though, because he was something, man. He was one of the first guys to latch onto it and to help promote it, you know, really. I always did admire him for that, because he wanted to play. I mean, like, he wanted to be in on everything that was new. He was in on it, and he wanted to be in on it.

And there were a lot of guys out there that really didn't like it, especially in California. People used to come by to hear Hawk, and they heard the band he had, and they'd tell me, 'Ah, why don't he play like he used to play?' and 'This ain't his thing.' Like, Kid Ory comes by and he said, 'Oh, man. This ain't the type of music I want to hear.' But I mean, we fixed him later on. He found out he couldn't hear it anyway, heh-heh. But I mean, he meant well. He just was into one type of thing, you know.
